title: Compiler fallback strategy — sync notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick sync notes from the architecture review on the proposed compiler-fallback strategy. Goal was to reconcile two competing objectives: 1) maximize fast-path coverage for compiled kernels to hit token-SLOs, and 2) guarantee graceful correctness/performance when compiled kernels fail (binary incompat, untested op, numeric drift). This doc captures alternatives discussed, measurements, and next steps.

Attendees:
- Maya Thompson (owner)
- Ravi Patel
- Lena Kim
- Diego Alvarez
- Sofia Rinehart
- Alex Osei (observability, joined for telemetry Qs)

Agenda:
1) Recap of RFC assumptions and constraints
2) Failure surface taxonomy (compile-time vs runtime vs hardware mismatch)
3) Proposed fallback modes and decision points
4) Telemetry/guardrails required for safe rollback
5) Canary rollout and experiment plan
6) Action items & owners

Recap / constraints:
- We expect ~78% of model shapes (seq len / batch) to be covered by compiled kernels for current model catalog. Remaining cases either require interpreter fallback or slower kernels.
- Private deployments may have older CUDA / driver stacks; must not crash inference process when precompiled kernels are incompatible.
- Correctness is non-negotiable for customer-facing tokens; small numeric deltas allowed but must be within quality monitoring thresholds.
- Latency SLO: 99th pct token latency budget per model variant; fallback must not silently breach SLO without triggering policy.

Failure taxonomy (short):
- Compile-time mismatch: kernel binary not loadable (ABI/drv incompat)
- Missing-op: compiled kernel doesn't cover a rare op sequence (e.g., fused op for custom layer)
- Numeric-regression: compiled kernel produces outputs with measurable drift for edge inputs
- Runtime crash/OOM: kernel triggers GPU fault under certain memory layouts

Fallback decision points discussed:
A) Pre-load/validate: on startup, attempt to load compiled kernels and run a small set of synthetic validate vectors to detect ABI/driver issues before serving live traffic. If validation fails, mark compiled group as disabled for that cluster.
B) Per-request fast-path check: lightweight capability bitmask per worker (seqLen bucket, batch size, model variant). Immediately route to compiled kernel if mask matches; otherwise use interpreter.
C) Dynamic runtime guardrail: if the compiled kernel is selected but produces outputs with anomalous histogram signatures (see telemetry section), immediately flag the worker and transition subsequent requests to interpreter for that model/variant.
D) Canary-first rollout: enable compiled kernels for X% of tokens/requests with enhanced monitoring and auto-rollback criteria.

Design alternatives (pros/cons):
1) Aggressive compile-and-deploy: compile full kernel set for all shapes and optimistically enable.
   - Pros: max perf coverage if successful.
   - Cons: brittle on heterogeneous infra; higher risk of mass failure.
2) Conservative: pre-validate on a small hardware matrix and only enable compiled kernels where validation passed.
   - Pros: safer, predictable.
   - Cons: slower to get perf wins, more complex per-cluster state.
3) Progressive per-request selection with fast fallthrough to interpreter (preferred hybrid).
   - Pros: best balance between perf and safety; graceful degradation within request path.
   - Cons: small added branching cost; requires careful telemetry to detect silent regressions.

Telemetry & observability requirements:
- Validation-run health events: successful/failed kernel loads + vector validation results (per cluster, per kernel hash).
- Runtime anomaly signals: per-request hash of output-feature histograms (reduced sketch), mean L2 drift relative to interpreter baseline for sample requests, and a small reservoir of diffs for deep analysis.
- Rate-limited crash traces and GPU-fault counters correlated with kernel-hash + model-variant.
- SLO breach alerts: if compiled path causes 5xx or p99 latency > baseline by >25% for >5m, trigger automated rollback for that variant.
- Canary dashboards: token-level split, quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE proxies or embedding cosine similarity against baseline), and cost delta.

Canary rollout plan (proposal):
Phase 0 — lab validation (today–1w): compile target kernels, run validation matrix across 3 driver versions (stable, recent, EOL) on internal infra. Responsible: Diego.
Phase 1 — cluster canary (1w): enable compiled kernels for internal dev clusters serving low-SLA traffic at 5% token allocation. Monitor for 48h with exit criteria: any crash / p99 > 3x baseline / mean embedding drift > 0.03. Responsible: Lena + SRE.
Phase 2 — customer canary (2–4w): gradually increase to 25% token allocation for non-critical tenants. Enable enhanced logging and diffs sampling. Responsible: Ravi + Solutions Eng.
Phase 3 — wide rollout (4–8w): if metrics pass, enable compiled kernels per model variant for clusters that passed pre-validation. Rollout must be reversible via feature flag. Responsible: Maya + Release Eng.

Safety mechanisms (must-have):
- Feature-flag gate per-cluster and per-model-variant with countdown/retry semantics.
- Auto-disable after N errors in M minutes with immediate telemetry dump.
- Fallback cache: maintain small LRU of recent interpreter outputs for identical prefixes to compare when a compiled path is first used (helps surface regressions quickly).
- Throttled golden comparisons: sample 1 in 10k tokens for deep diff and push to eval pipeline.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Q1: How to represent output-histogram sketch compactly and deterministically across worker languages? (Ravi to propose wire format)
- Q2: Thresholds for numeric drift (embedding cosine cutoff) are model-dependent; need a mapping table per catalog entry. Who owns this mapping? (Product + Applied ML)
- Q3: Policy for private/on-prem older drivers — should we auto-compile a compatibility shim or simply mark compiled kernels disabled?
- Q4: Operational cost impact — compiled kernels reduce token-time but increase memory usage; need updated cost model to decide when to enable by default.

Benchmarks shared during meeting (summary):
- Model A (base-large, seq=512): compiled kernel p50 token time: 7.2ms vs interpreter 12.8ms (≈44% improvement). p99 improvement smaller (30%) due to tail scheduling.
- Model B (decoder-only, varying seq): compiled kernels help heavily for seq <= 256 but degrade for batched long sequences due to specialized memory layout.
- Observed rare kernel-load failure on old driver stack (n=3 in 120 validation runs on driver 11.0).

Decisions made in meeting (explicit):
1) Adopt the hybrid approach (#3 above): pre-validate at cluster start + per-request selection + runtime guardrail. (agreed, 5-0)
2) Implement feature-flag and auto-disable policy as required gating for rollout. (agreed)
3) Build small LRU fallback-cache for recent interpreter outputs to enable quick comparison and warm-starting. (agreed, Diego to prototype)
4) Telemetry schema will be proposed by Ravi; Alex will validate feasibility with current observability pipeline. (agreed)

Action items (owner — due):
- Diego: lab validation matrix + prototype fallback LRU (due 2024-11-15)
- Ravi: telemetry message spec (compact histogram sketch, drift counters) + sample event size estimate (due 2024-11-14)
- Lena: canary orchestration runbook draft with exit criteria + alert thresholds (due 2024-11-18)
- Sofia: cost model update draft for enabling compiled kernels (due 2024-11-20)
- Maya: update RFC with chosen hybrid design and link to this doc + schedule implementation checkpoints (due 2024-11-13)

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- We should align with product catalog owners to get a per-model quality threshold matrix (Q2).
- Consider adding a small on-disk compiled-kernel signing step to prevent accidental bad binaries being deployed. Could integrate with platform-engineering model signing RFC.
- Keep experimental flags hidden behind 'internal-canary' until Phase 2.

Appendix (short pointers):
- Example: failure vector used for validation: random input seeds 42/123/999 across sequence buckets [64, 128, 256, 512], compare logits distribution mean/std and embedding cosine to interpreter baseline.
- Related PR: runtime/#1123 contains initial kernel hashing + load API.

End of notes.
